import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 364

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/364](https://www.erdosproblems.com/364)
-/

open Nat

namespace Erdos364

/-- There is no consecutive triple of powerful numbers. -/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_364 :
    ¬ ∃ (n : ℕ), Powerful n ∧ Powerful (n + 1) ∧ Powerful (n + 2) := by
  sorry

/--
Erdős [Er76d] conjectured a stronger statement: if $n_k$ is the $k$th powerful number,
then $n_{k+2} - n_k > n_k^c$ for some constant $c > 0$.

[Er76d] Erdős, P., Problems and results on number theoretic properties of consecutive integers and related questions. Proceedings of the Fifth Manitoba Conference on Numerical Mathematics (Univ. Manitoba, Winnipeg, Man., 1975) (1976), 25-44.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_364.variants.strong :
    ∃ (c : ℝ) (h : c > 0), ∀ (k : ℕ),
    Nat.nth Powerful (k + 2) - Nat.nth Powerful k > (Nat.nth Powerful k : ℝ) ^ c := by
  sorry

/--
There is no quadruple of powerful numbers, since at least one of the four numbers must be
$2 \pmod{4}$, which cannot be powerful (since $2$ divides it, but $2^2$ does not).
-/
@[category textbook, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_364.variants.weak :
    ¬ ∃ (n : ℕ), Powerful n ∧ Powerful (n + 1) ∧ Powerful (n + 2) ∧ Powerful (n + 3) := by
  intro h
  obtain ⟨n, hn⟩ := h
  have h2mod4 : n % 4 = 2 ∨ (n + 1) % 4 = 2 ∨ (n + 2) % 4 = 2 ∨ (n + 3) % 4 = 2 := by omega
  rcases h2mod4 with (_|_|_|_) <;>
  simp_all [not_full_of_prime_mod_prime_sq _ 1 (Nat.prime_two)]

end Erdos364

reformulations.difference: The source specifies positive integers, whereas Lean allows n = 0 and Nat.Powerful includes zero.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The only additional starting point is n = 0, whose triple contains 2, which is not powerful. Thus the existential statements over natural and positive starting points are equivalent, as are their negations. Also verified that Nat.Powerful agrees with the prime-square divisibility definition.

reformulations.difference: Nat.nth Powerful enumerates 0, 1, 4, 8, …, rather than just the positive powerful numbers.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Writing a(k) = Nat.nth Powerful k and b(k) for the zero-indexed positive powerful numbers, proved a(k + 1) = b(k). Consequently every inequality with k ≥ 1 is exactly a reindexed source inequality. The additional k = 0 inequality is 4 > 0^c, automatically true for c > 0. Proved the full equivalence of the two existential gap statements.

reformulations.difference: The Lean quadruple statement also allows zero as a starting point.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The extra quadruple 0, 1, 2, 3 contains the non-powerful number 2. Restricting starting points to positive integers therefore gives an equivalent assertion.

sources_consulted: P. Erdős, Problems and results on number theoretic properties of consecutive integers and related questions (1976), pp. 25–44, section on powerful numbers: https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1976-39.pdf
review.notes: All three declarations are mathematically faithful. The source explicitly records Erdős's negative conjecture and still lists the problem as open; the recent results mentioned concern restricted cases. Inspected Nat.Full/Powerful, primeFactors, Nat.nth, and real exponentiation. Proved infinitude of powerful numbers using squares, ruling out Nat.nth's missing-element default, and confirmed that the gap subtraction elaborates over ℝ. Computed small powerful numbers and checked all triple starting points below 2000, finding none. /workspace/review/scratch.lean compiles; the equivalence proofs and the existing quadruple proof have no sorryAx dependency. Source HTML and the original paper's extracted text were obtained through r.jina.ai; direct Erdős Problems requests encountered Cloudflare challenges. The reviewed file was not modified.
